subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Frederick the Great vs. Coffee
description: A 60-second lesson on Frederick the Great vs. Coffee.

hook.text: Prussia's Frederick the Great tried to ban common people from drinking coffee in 1777—insisting they drink beer instead.

buildup.text: Frederick argued that coffee drained money from the Prussian economy. He feared rising imports would bankrupt the state.

discovery.text: He created 'coffee sniffers'—government agents who roamed streets, sniffing for the aroma of illegal home coffee roasting.

twist.text: The policy was wildly unpopular and impossible to enforce. Citizens roasted in secret, like prohibition later.

climax.text: Frederick himself was a notorious coffee lover. He drank it daily—brewed with champagne instead of water, by some accounts.

punchline.text: A king who banned coffee but drank it himself. Hypocrisy brewed perfectly.

quiz.question: What were 'coffee sniffers' in Frederick the Great's Prussia?
options: Government agents who sniffed for illegal home coffee roasting
